findings.title: Raw signup request body (including plaintext password) is logged
findings.explanation: `req.body` on the signup route contains the plaintext password, email (PII) and organization. The PR claims the logger redacts sensitive fields, but this is a fragile assumption: redaction is typically key-name based and may not be applied to nested objects, differently named fields (e.g. `pass`, `passwd`, `confirmPassword`, `newPassword`), or unexpected shapes. Invalid signups are exactly the case where clients send malformed or unexpected payloads, so the redaction is least likely to match there. Users also often mistype or put a password in the wrong field (e.g. in the email field), which would then be written to logs, log aggregators and backups. Remove the raw body log. Instead log a safe, allow-listed summary such as which keys were present, their types and lengths, and a boolean for whether the email looks valid, or log the zod validation error (issues contain paths and codes, not values) when validation fails.

findings.title: Logging happens before validation, so arbitrary unvalidated, unbounded client input is written to logs
findings.explanation: The payload is logged before `signupSchema.parse`, so any unauthenticated caller can write arbitrarily large or crafted content (very large bodies, log-injection strings, deeply nested objects) into the logs. That risks log volume/cost abuse, storage blowup, and polluted log data. If body logging is truly needed, log only after validation of the shape, truncate, and use an allow-list of fields.

findings.title: Debugging goal is better served by logging validation failures
findings.explanation: The stated goal is to understand why signups fail validation. `signupSchema.parse` throws a ZodError; catching it (or using `safeParse`) and logging `error.issues` (field paths, error codes, messages) answers 'why did it fail' without logging any values. It would also let the route return a proper 400 with field errors instead of relying on a generic error handler (verify that an unhandled ZodError does not become a 500). This also logs only failures rather than every signup attempt, cutting volume.

findings.title: Log level and message not suited for every signup attempt
findings.explanation: `info` for every attempt, with full payloads, is noisy and gets retained at default production levels. If any temporary diagnostic logging is kept, use `debug` or `warn` on failure only, and add a request ID/correlation ID so entries can be tied to responses without including the payload.

findings.title: No test covering the redaction assumption
findings.explanation: If the team relies on the logger's redaction, add a test that asserts password and email fields are masked for this route's payload shape (including nested and misnamed keys). Better still, avoid depending on it by not logging the body.
